title: Sasol to close VCM and PVC facilities
summary: Sasolburg, South Africa – Sasol will discontinue operations at its Vinyl Chloride Monomer (VCM) and Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) facilities at its Sasol Midland site in Sasolburg. Production is scheduled to cease at the end of June 2027. The decision follows a review of the Chlor-Vinyls value chain at Sasol’s Sasolburg Operations. The review concluded that the aging VCM and PVC assets are no longer economically viable and are adversely affecting the company's free cash flow.
body_markdown:
# Overview


Through proprietary technologies and processes the main products Sasol produces are fuel components, chemical components and co-products. From these main products and further value-adding processes we deliver diesel, petrol (gasoline), naphtha, kerosene (jet fuel), liquid petroleum gas (LPG), olefins, alcohols, polymers, solvents, surfactants, co-monomers, ammonia, methanol, crude tar acids, sulphur, illuminating paraffin, bitumen and fuel oil. Even further processing produces numerous additional products.
